title: GEM: Geometric Erasure by Contrastive Velocity Matching in Rectified Flows
abstract: arXiv:2606.00140v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: While the rapid adoption of multimodal generative models offers immense potential, it has also increased the risks of harmful content synthesis, deepfakes, and copyright infringements. To address these challenges, concept erasure has emerged as a prospective safeguard. However, as the field gradually transitions from U-Net-based diffusion models to Rectified Flow Transformers, erasure research has struggled to keep pace. In this work, we introduce GEM, a simple but highly effective erasure framework for Rectified Flow models. As part of our contribution, we establish a principled bridge between trajectory-based unlearning grounded in Generative Flow Networks and classic teacher-guided erasure: we translate trajectory-based signals into a teacher-guided flow-matching setup that unifies the strengths of both paradigms. translated_title: GEM：基于对比速度匹配的修正流几何擦除
translated_abstract: arXiv:2606.00140v3 公告类型：交叉替换 摘要：虽然多模态生成模型的快速普及提供了巨大潜力，但也增加了有害内容合成、深度伪造和版权侵权的风险。为了应对这些挑战，概念擦除已成为一种有前景的防护手段。然而，随着该领域逐渐从基于U-Net的扩散模型转向修正流变换器，擦除研究一直难以跟上步伐。在这项工作中，我们引入了GEM，一个简单但高效的修正流模型擦除框架。作为我们贡献的一部分，我们建立了基于生成流网络的轨迹级反学习与经典教师引导擦除之间的原则性桥梁：我们将轨迹级信号转化为教师引导的流匹配设置，统一了两种范式的优势。具体而言，教师提供互补的吸引和排斥信号，我们将其合并为一个几何信号。
tldr: GEM通过将轨迹级反学习信号转化为教师引导的流匹配设置，为修正流模型提供了一种统一吸引与排斥信号的简单高效概念擦除方法。
en_tdlr: GEM provides a simple yet effective concept erasure framework for Rectified Flow models by translating trajectory-based unlearning signals into a teacher-guided flow-matching setup that unifies attraction and repulsion signals.
